summary: Anton Schiefner (1817–1879) was a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and Indology. He studied law at Saint Petersburg State University (~1836–1840) and served as a librarian (Bibliothekar) at the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1852–1879).

Anton Westermann (1806–1869) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig University (~1823–1826) and later held a post there from ~1834 to 1869, teaching Friedrich Max Müller.

Antonino Forte (1940–2006) specialized in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at EFEO (~1976–1989), Hōbōgirin (~1976–1986), Scuola Italiana di Studi sull'Asia Orientale (~1982–1999; attested 1996–2003), and the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~1989–2006).
Antonio T. de Nicolás (1930–2022) worked in philosophy and Indology. He studied at Fordham University (~1967–1971) and held a position at Stony Brook University from ~1969 to 1996.

Antonio Terrone works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned a PhD at Leiden University (-2010) under Tilmann Vetter and Barend ter Haar, also studying under other teachers, and served as scholar in residence at BDRC.

Anukul Chandra Banerjee was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Calcutta, where he was Assistant Lecturer in Pali (attested 1943), and served as Director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (attested 1981).

Archibald Edward Gough (1845–1915) worked in Indology and philosophy, studying under Monier Monier-Williams. He held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1868–1878), Presidency University, Kolkata (~1878–1895, attested 1914), and Aliah University (~1881–1895, attested 1914).

Arindam Chakrabarti is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who earned a DPhil at the University of Oxford. He held professorships at the University of Delhi (attested 1999) and the University of Hawaii (attested 2009–2012, 2014).
Arinde L. Jonker is an Indology scholar who completed a Research MA at Leiden University (attested 2018) under supervisor Peter Bisschop, also studying under Jonathan A. Silk.
Aristotle C. Dy specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed a PhD at SOAS University of London (attested 2013) under the doctoral supervision of Antonello Palumbo.

Arjo Vanderjagt (1948–) is a scholar in philosophy. He studied at the University of Groningen (1971–1981) and held academic posts at Radboud University (1976–1979), the University of Groningen (1994–2009), and Utrecht University (2007).

Arlo Griffiths (1976–) is an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Leiden University (~1999–2004). He held posts at the University of Groningen (~2003–2005), Leiden University (attested 2002–2008), and the École française d'Extrême-Orient (from 2008).
Arnold Hermann Ludwig Heeren (1760–1842) was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at the University of Göttingen (~1779–1784) and later served as a professor there from ~1794 to 1842.

Arthur Anthony Macdonell (1854–1930) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Göttingen, Oxford, and Leipzig. He served as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (1899) and was a Fellow at Balliol College (~1899–1926).

Arthur Berriedale Keith (1879–1944) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Edinburgh and Balliol College under Arthur Anthony Macdonell, worked at the Colonial Office (~1901–1914), and served as Regius Professor at Edinburgh (~1914–1944).

Arthur Christensen (1875–1945) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Copenhagen (~1893–1903) and was appointed professor extraordinarius of Iranian philology there in 1919.
Arthur Coke Burnell (1840–1882) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Bedford School and King's College London (~1857–1860) before serving in the Indian Civil Service from ~1860 to 1882.

Arthur F. Wright (1913–1976) was a scholar of Sinology, history, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Stanford, Oxford, and Harvard, and served as Charles Seymour Professor of History at Yale University from ~1961 to 1976.

Arthur Llewellyn Basham (1914–1986) was a historian and Indologist who studied at SOAS. He was a professor at the University of London and SOAS, and later served as a department head at Australian National University (~1965–1978).
Arthur McKeown is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Harvard University (attested 2005) under Parimal G. Patil, Palri Sangye, and Diana L. Eck.
